findings.reason: it is context describing what grew the file, no node acts on it, and it does not change any deliverable or gate.
findings.text: "the growth came from gc sweeps, the worktree-release work, a-held §16 and a-run-has-one-live-writer §2" abbreviates a plan to "a-held", which four distinct plans match (`a-held-blocker-clears-on-its-probe`, `a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn`, `a-held-session-routes-to-a-serving-lane`, and this plan's own sibling), so the reader cannot tell which §16 is meant

findings.reason: a node taking the enumerated bullet as the authoritative list moves twelve names instead of fourteen, leaving `_write_sender_record` and `_running_descendants` in `routing.py`, which re-inflates the file toward the 50,000-token bound the section exists to clear and wastes a run on a done-when that then finds `estimated_tokens` still over.
findings.text: the process-signalling bullet enumerates the family as "`signal_worker`, `_signal_one`, `_signal_process_group`, `_run_process_pids`, `_processes_owning_run`, `_process_environment`, `_start_tick`, `_worker_record`, `_recorded_worker_pid`, `_run_launch_floor`, `_root_names_the_recorded_process`, `RUN_ID_ENV`, and the constants only this family reads, `SENDER_RECORD_NAME` and `_RUN_WORKER_RECORD`", but the import-edges paragraph then says "`_write_sender_record` and `_running_descendants` move with the process-signalling family" — two functions absent from the enumeration, and neither appears anywhere else in the section's name list (both are real family members: `_write_sender_record` at `routing.py:3197` is called only from `_signal_one`/`_signal_process_group`, `_running_descendants` at `routing.py:3356` only from `_run_process_pids`)
